answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent registrations to progressive cryptographic stake burning. An agent anchor acts like an economic wharf where identity stakes are permanently destroyed. For $n$ identities created by an entity, burning costs scale superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$, turning Sybil replication hollow and financially ruinous. Attackers trying to fracture consensus like brittle shale face an unviable quadratic wall.
